name: Javi López, Borja Giménez Larraz - § 38 - Am 26
title: INTERIM REPORT in view of the consent procedure on the Political, Economic and Cooperation Strategic Partnership Agreement between the EU and Mexico
part_text: 38. Recognises Mexico’s growing importance as both an expanding market and a strategic partner in the supply of critical raw materials; notes Mexico’s vital role as a producer of critical raw materials, particularly as the source of 33 % of the EU’s fluorspar imports, which is critical for the steel, iron and refrigeration supply chains; expresses concern that the Agreement reflects an EU approach focused on securing access to raw materials without a strategy to reduce overall resource consumption; warns that the EU’s continued and unsustainable pursuit of external raw material supplies risks perpetuating patterns of neo-extractivism and reinforcing the EU’s structural dependency on imported raw materials and goods, rather than addressing underlying demand; stresses that provisions such as the prohibition of export monopolies and the ban on dual pricing significantly constrain Mexico’s ability to pursue domestic industrial policies, develop local value chains and ensure the fair distribution of resource wealth; regrets the lack of binding safeguards for environmental protection, indigenous rights and local communities; calls for EU and Mexican authorities to ensure that the Agreement effectively promotes compliance with the highest sustainability standards in the extraction and processing of raw materials, and that all mining projects enabled by the Agreement meaningfully involve and contribute to delivering tangible benefits to local and indigenous communities; calls for the EU to actively support Mexico in its efforts to move up the value chain, as well as in enhancing social, environmental and human rights standards in the mining sector; calls for a fundamental reorientation of trade policy towards reducing resource dependency, promoting circular economy approaches and ensuring that raw material partnerships are based on sustainability, equity and support for value addition in third countries;
